meta.name: ACF Glossary
meta.purpose: Single source of truth for inline tooltip content across all six framework parts and for the /glossary reference index, which is GENERATED from this file (scripts/build-glossary-page.mjs). Tooltips and the index are populated from this file; never hand-author a second glossary.

schema.id: stable slug, used as the data key and tooltip anchor (kebab-case)
schema.aliases: alternate spellings/phrasings the tagger should also match
schema.context: OPTIONAL sense guard. A one-word term is a word first and a term second, so a term listed here is only auto-tagged in a block that also carries one of these words. Added 2026-09-16 after 'the framework stops describing' was tagged as Stop-loss, 'margin expansion' as margin borrowing, and 'sector rotation' as posture Rotation. Use it whenever the term or an alias is a common English word with another meaning; prefer it over deleting an alias that is right somewhere else.
schema.wave: 1 to 4 = rollout pass (1 = first pass, highest comprehension value; 2 = second pass; 3 = domain terms; 4 = named concepts added 2026-09-15)
schema.category: closed key from meta.categories; groups the /glossary index (explicit, never derived from appearsLater)
schema.definition: layer-one tooltip copy: concise, plain-English, no em dashes
schema.length: short | medium: sizing hint for the tooltip card

source.ref: internal -> 'Part N · <Title>' of the Part that teaches it; external -> primary or academic citation

schema.related: layer-two: sibling concept ids whose roots should wake on hover (the mycelium adjacency)
schema.appearsLater: layer-two: the part where this term becomes operational ('see where this appears later')
schema.chart: id of the chart in the chart-handoff inventory that substantiates this term, if any

meta.usage: Tooltip layer one shows 'definition'. Layer two ('see where this appears later') is built from 'appearsLater' + 'related'. The 'related' and 'chart' ids share vocabulary with the chart-handoff CONNECTS-TO network so the glossary and the charts form one cross-reference graph. Internal sources cite the framework's own Parts; external sources cite primary/academic references.
meta.harmonizeNote: Carry vectors harmonized 2026-07-26 and corrected 2026-09-30: the carry-vector entry defines the closed structure label (Long Carry | Short Carry | Barbell), which is not an input to the carry-direction sub-score inside the CIS macro component (Part 6). Power-law corridor was harmonized against Part 3 earlier.

terms.definition: A payoff that curves upward: a favorable move earns more than an equal adverse move costs. The framework sizes and places every position to keep that shape, and Part 6 scores how well each one holds it.

source.ref: Part 2 · Lineage & Macro Thesis (lineage); defined on the cover; scored in Part 6 · Convexity & Framework Integrity Scoring

appearsLater.topic: How convexity is expressed through Posture

terms.definition: Convexity Integrity Score: a 0 to 100 score for one position at a time, built from four components: convexity and optionality, risk and fragility, macro alignment, and execution and sentiment. The dashboard computes it, and Part 6 defines it. CIS below 50 removes allocation eligibility for a position in any of the three postures; Bitcoin answers to Part 3.

A falsifiable view of the structural forces likely to shape markets over the next 5 to 20 years, which sets the portfolio's structure. It assigns probabilities across regime scenarios rather than making a point forecast.

appearsLater.topic: The lineage and the full regime thesis

terms.definition: A predefined threshold that triggers a review before denial, emotion or information overload can take over. The dashboard detects and displays; the response is yours.

source.ref: Part 1 · Foundation & Philosophy; Part 5 · Portfolio Construction & Position Management

terms.definition: A trend-validation rule: the market must confirm a thesis before it carries full size, and when all three momentum dimensions turn negative the position exits even with a high CIS. The dashboard does not yet measure the three dimensions.

source.ref: Part 5 · Portfolio Construction & Position Management; Moskowitz, Ooi & Pedersen (2012), 'Time Series Momentum', Journal of Financial Economics 104(2); Hurst, Ooi & Pedersen (2017), 'A Century of Evidence on Trend-Following Investing', Journal of Portfolio Management 44(1)

terms.definition: The type of account a holding sits in: Roth, taxable or pre-tax, each with its own tax rules. Over decades the wrapper can change what you keep by a wide margin, so the framework decides placement as deliberately as it picks positions; Parts 4 and 5 work the arithmetic.

source.ref: Part 4 · Tax Architecture & ROC Strategy; IRS Publications 590-A and 590-B

terms.definition: The posture for high-upside positions in regime forces that are real, durable and capital-backed, yet still early or underowned by institutions. Torque carries the portfolio's upside and absorbs its deepest drawdowns, which can reach 50 to 70 percent in liquidity stress, so each position has to earn its size through its score.

The reserve posture: positions built to hold steady through liquidity stress, policy error or a narrative reversal, then supply the capital to buy the dislocation. Aggregate Ballast stays at or above 15 percent, and yield alone never qualifies a position (see Ballast eligibility).

Narrative-driven convexity with weak structural backing. Useful only under hard caps and an exit committed to before entry. The caps are 5 percent a position and 10 percent in aggregate, and the stop sits 15 to 25 percent below entry.

appearsLater.topic: The Hype posture and its limits

terms.definition: A condition in which government debt and the cost of financing it, rather than the inflation goal, start to dictate what monetary policy can do. Part 1 reads it in the interest bill: by 2025 federal interest was back at about 3.2 percent of GDP, level with its 1991 peak, on more than twice the debt.

source.ref: Sargent & Wallace (1981), 'Some Unpleasant Monetarist Arithmetic', Federal Reserve Bank of Minneapolis Quarterly Review 5(3); FRED (OMB) series FYOIGDA188S and FYPUGDA188S; Part 1 · Foundation & Philosophy

appearsLater.topic: The macro thesis and policy backdrop

terms.definition: Holding appreciated assets instead of selling them, borrowing against them for cash, and leaving them to heirs, who under current US law receive a stepped-up basis, so the gain built up during life may never be taxed as income; the loan is repaid from the estate. It works for any appreciated capital asset, depends on current law and on credit staying available, and carries interest cost and liquidation risk.

source.ref: Part 3 · Bitcoin: Convexity Backbone (TAM, custody, and the borrow phase); IRC §1014

terms.definition: Harm that grows faster than the shock causing it, so one large shock does more damage than several small ones of the same total size. The framework keeps it apart from volatility, and CIS scores it in the Risk and Fragility component.

source.ref: Taleb & Douady (2013), 'Mathematical definition, mapping, and detection of (anti)fragility', Quantitative Finance 13(11)

terms.definition: The behavioral class every position except Bitcoin carries: Torque, Ballast or Hype. It sets the position's sizing table and governance rules, and it classifies how a holding behaves, whatever kind of asset it is. Bitcoin sits outside all three, under Part 3's rules.

Reflexivity, in Soros's sense, is the loop in which beliefs and prices change the fundamentals they are supposed to reflect. Policy reflexivity adds policymakers to the loop: they react to markets, markets react back, and the feedback can amplify instability in either direction.

source.ref: Soros, The Alchemy of Finance (1987); Part 1 · Foundation & Philosophy; Part 2 · Lineage & Macro Thesis

terms.definition: The tendency of large price moves to follow large moves, and calm to follow calm, so turbulence arrives in stretches rather than as one isolated shock. A risk plan sized for an average week can be undersized for the weeks that follow a shock.

source.ref: Mandelbrot (1963), 'The Variation of Certain Speculative Prices', Journal of Business 36(4); Engle (1982), autoregressive conditional heteroscedasticity (ARCH), Econometrica 50(4); Part 1 · Foundation & Philosophy

appearsLater.topic: The traditional playbook is failing quietly

terms.definition: The tendency of the relationship between asset classes to change with the regime. From roughly 2000 to 2021 stocks and bonds tended to move in opposite directions, so bonds cushioned equity losses; in 2021 and 2022 the correlation turned positive again, and in 2022 both fell together.

source.ref: Lombardi & Sushko (2023), 'The correlation of equity and bond returns', BIS Quarterly Review, December 2023, Box A; Brixton, Brooks, Hecht, Ilmanen, Maloney & McQuinn (2023), 'A Changing Stock-Bond Correlation: Drivers and Implications', Journal of Portfolio Management 49(4)

terms.definition: The framework's objective: compounding that keeps going because the portfolio can survive being wrong about timing, size or outcome while keeping enough exposure to convex payoffs. Staying in the game comes first, since a large gain cannot rescue capital that was forced out before it arrived.

Rare, very large gains: the few outcomes that can account for most of a convex portfolio's lifetime return. Because so much rides on them, the account they are realized in (Part 4) matters more for them than for an ordinary gain.

source.ref: Part 1 · Foundation & Philosophy; Part 4 · Tax Architecture & ROC Strategy

terms.definition: An AI-assisted research step the practitioner runs after a tripwire fires to speed evidence-gathering, without handing final judgment to the machine.

Total addressable market: how much money a market could plausibly bring to an asset. For a company it is the market it could serve, set against its current value, which CIS scores as headroom; for Bitcoin, Part 3 estimates the share of existing monetary assets it could absorb. It sizes potential; it does not forecast a price.

source.ref: Part 3 · Bitcoin: Convexity Backbone; Part 6 · Convexity & Framework Integrity Scoring

appearsLater.topic: The conservative addressable-market estimate for the Bitcoin reserve

terms.definition: A band around a power-law trend: on log-log axes (log price against log days since the genesis block), Bitcoin's price has historically tracked a straight line, with spikes above it and capitulations below. The framework reads it as context for accumulation pace, not a price prediction. No line in it is a hard floor: Bitcoin spent most of February to mid-September 2026 below the dashboard's floor line.

source.ref: Part 3 · Bitcoin: Convexity Backbone; Santostasi, price-time power law (Reddit, 2018; Medium, 2024); Burger (2019), 'Bitcoin's natural long-term power-law corridor of growth', Medium

terms.definition: The risk that the order of returns, not just their average, decides the outcome once money is flowing out or in. For someone withdrawing, early losses force sales at low prices and leave less capital for the recovery to work on; with no cash flows, the same returns in any order end at the same value.

source.ref: Part 1 · Foundation & Philosophy; Part 3 · Bitcoin: Convexity Backbone

terms.definition: A structure that pairs very safe holdings with a small, highly convex allocation and skips the fragile middle. It aims for payoff asymmetry rather than low volatility. In the dashboard, Barbell is also one of the three structure labels a position can carry (see Carry vectors).

source.ref: Taleb, The Black Swan (2007) and Antifragile (2012); Part 2 · Lineage & Macro Thesis

terms.definition: Buying a fixed amount on a set schedule regardless of price, which spreads entry risk across time. The framework funds it from income, raises it about 50 percent when valuation models converge on a deep discount, and slows discretionary buying during extensions.

Cash held ready to deploy into dislocations. It comes from two places: income held back from discretionary Bitcoin buying during extensions (Part 3), and Ballast distributions that build up between deployments and are spent in stress (Part 5).

source.ref: Part 3 · Bitcoin: Convexity Backbone; Part 5 · Portfolio Construction & Position Management

terms.definition: A distribution treated as a return of your own invested capital rather than as income, a characterization set each tax year that can change. It is not taxed when received but lowers your cost basis, deferring the tax until you sell, unless a step-up at death resets the basis first under current law. Once basis reaches zero, further return-of-capital distributions are taxed as capital gains when received.

source.ref: Part 4 · Tax Architecture & ROC Strategy; IRC §301(c); Form 1099-DIV, Box 3

terms.definition: Framework Integrity Score: a score out of 100 for the portfolio as a whole, measuring how closely its construction follows the framework's rules. FIS starts the assembled portfolio at 100 and deducts capped, named penalties in five buckets: allocation (25), governance (15), dead capital (15), concentration (15) and complexity (10, hard cap). The caps sum to 80, so a valid FIS cannot fall below 20.

The closed structure label every position carries: Long Carry (pro-liquidity, duration-sensitive growth that works when financial conditions ease), Short Carry (hard assets, defense and inflation or geopolitical stress plays that work when carry breaks), or Barbell (small positions with fat-tail optionality and discontinuous upside). Separately, the CIS Macro component has a carry-direction sub-score; the label is not an input to it.

source.ref: ACF dashboard · structure labels (software behavior as of September 2026); Part 6 · Convexity & Framework Integrity Scoring

appearsLater.topic: Carry direction inside the CIS macro component

terms.definition: An account funded with after-tax money whose qualified withdrawals are tax-free, so gains compound and positions can be sold inside it without tax. The framework treats its annual capacity as scarce and spends it on Torque that may rotate. Bitcoin, which is never sold, sits outside it by default.

An ordinary brokerage account with no contribution limit, where gains are taxed when you sell and distributions in the year they are paid. The framework places never-sold Bitcoin here, along with return-of-capital Ballast, buy-and-hold positions beyond Roth capacity, and harvesting satellites. Bitcoin belongs here by default: held to death it passes with a stepped-up basis under current law, and only a taxable holding can be pledged for a loan.

source.ref: Part 4 · Tax Architecture & ROC Strategy; Part 3 · Bitcoin: Convexity Backbone

terms.definition: An account funded before tax: contributions lower your taxable income now, and withdrawals are taxed as ordinary income. At equal tax rates in and out, Roth and pre-tax end even. For convex, right-tail positions the balance tips toward Roth because contribution limits are set in dollars, required distributions can push large pre-tax balances into higher brackets, and heirs generally inherit a Roth free of income tax under current law (Part 4).

A way to fund a Roth IRA when your income is above the limit for contributing directly: contribute to a traditional IRA without deducting it, then convert. It works under current law, and the pro-rata rule taxes part of the conversion if you hold other pre-tax IRA money at year-end.

source.ref: Part 4 · Tax Architecture & ROC Strategy; IRS Form 8606

terms.definition: A withdrawal the law requires each year from pre-tax retirement accounts. RMDs start at age 73, or at 75 for anyone born in 1960 or later, under current rules. They create taxable income whether or not you need it, one reason the framework favors Roth, which requires none from its original owner, for long-horizon convex positions.

source.ref: Part 4 · Tax Architecture & ROC Strategy; IRS Publication 590-B

terms.definition: A 3.8 percent federal tax on net investment income, owed on the smaller of that income or the amount by which modified adjusted gross income exceeds $200,000 (single) or $250,000 (married filing jointly). The thresholds are not indexed for inflation. Qualified Roth withdrawals are not subject to it, part of why a taxable account keeps less of a large gain than a Roth.

The profit from selling a holding for more than its cost basis; in a taxable account it is taxed in the year you sell. Under current federal law a gain held more than a year is taxed at 0, 15 or 20 percent, plus the 3.8 percent NIIT at higher incomes (23.8 percent at the top), while a gain held a year or less is taxed as ordinary income. That gap, and the account the holding sits in, decide how much of a gain you keep.

What a holding counts as having cost you for tax purposes, usually the price paid plus fees. Your gain or loss on a sale is measured from it, return-of-capital distributions lower it, and under current law heirs generally receive it stepped up to the value at death.

The reset of an inherited asset's cost basis to its value at the owner's death under current US law (IRC §1014), so the gain built up during the owner's life is not taxed as income. Gifts made during life keep the giver's basis, and pre-tax retirement accounts get no step-up: heirs owe income tax on what they withdraw. It is policy-dependent, and it is one reason the framework holds never-sold Bitcoin in a taxable account.

source.ref: IRC 26 U.S.C. §1014 and §1015; Part 3 · Bitcoin: Convexity Backbone; Part 4 · Tax Architecture & ROC Strategy

terms.definition: Selling a holding at a loss on purpose to offset realized gains, plus up to $3,000 of ordinary income a year ($1,500 if married filing separately), while keeping similar exposure through a holding that is not substantially identical. Net losses beyond that carry forward to later years. The replacement starts at a lower basis, so much of the benefit is a deferral.

source.ref: Part 4 · Tax Architecture & ROC Strategy; IRC §1211(b) and §1212(b)

terms.definition: A rule that disallows a loss on stock or securities if you buy substantially identical ones within 30 days before or after the sale, in any of your accounts. The disallowed loss is normally added to the replacement's basis, so it is deferred, but a repurchase inside an IRA or Roth IRA loses it for good. Directly held Bitcoin is not covered under current law; H.R. 10357, advanced by the House Ways and Means Committee on September 16, 2026, would extend the rule to digital assets if enacted, and it is not law.

source.ref: IRC 26 U.S.C. §1091; Rev. Rul. 2008-5; IRS Publication 550; H.R. 10357, Digital Asset Tax Certainty Act (committee vote 38 to 5, September 16, 2026)

terms.definition: Deferring income into a pre-tax 401(k) or 403(b) in an unusually high-income year, then converting it to Roth or withdrawing it in a later year taxed at a lower rate. The value captured is the spread between the two marginal rates. A traditional IRA usually cannot carry it, because the deduction phases out in such a year for anyone covered by a workplace plan.
What the portfolio leaves you at the end of the horizon, after taxes, fees and other frictions. The framework judges decisions by it rather than by any single year's return.

appearsLater.topic: Wrapper engineering as a structural edge

terms.definition: How much capital a single position may carry. In this framework size is earned: the posture sets the band table, the score selects the band within it, and concentration limits cap the result at the household level.

The size range a CIS score earns within its posture's table. For Torque, 70 and above is core, 60 to 69 standard, 50 to 59 a starter, and below 50 nothing; Ballast uses the same cut points with smaller ranges (its 50 to 59 band is marginal), and Hype is simply eligible from 50 at 2 to 5 percent.

A ceiling on how much of the household portfolio, summed across every account, a single position or a small group may hold. Fifteen percent is the default single-position cap and 18 percent the absolute maximum, reachable only with a documented override (Part 5 doctrine); the top three stay within 35 percent and the top five within 50, with Bitcoin excluded. The dashboard flags breaches on the book you hold and does not block trades.

A fall from a prior peak, measured as the percentage lost from the high. The framework treats a survivable drawdown as the toll convex positions charge, provided position size and reserves let you hold through it.

source.ref: Part 1 · Foundation & Philosophy; Part 5 · Portfolio Construction & Position Management

terms.definition: How widely and how often a price moves, usually measured as the standard deviation of returns. The framework keeps it apart from fragility: a position can swing hard and still be robust, and what matters is whether a move can force you out.

Whether a position or portfolio can come through stress without a forced sale or a decision that ends the compounding. For a single position, CIS scores it in the Risk and Fragility component, where a higher score means less fragile.

Moving capital between postures as conditions change: trimming Torque after a run to rebuild Ballast, then deploying Ballast into Torque during dislocations. It is the framework's primary way of buying low without raising outside cash.

An exit price set before you buy. Every Hype position carries one, 15 to 25 percent below entry, and Part 5 forbids widening it or reclassifying the position to avoid honoring it. Placing and honoring the stop is yours: the dashboard places no orders, though it flags a Hype position 25 percent or more below cost.

The rule for exposure around a scheduled earnings report: from five trading days before it (T-5), a position may hold no more than 3 percent of the portfolio, because one report can move a stock 10 to 30 percent either way and conviction predicts none of it. The dashboard flags a position above the cap in the days before its report, but it counts calendar days, so the flag can arrive a trading day or two after T-5; start the trim from the earnings calendar. It trims nothing: the trim is yours, and so is the T-21 to T-6 blackout on opening new positions.

appearsLater.topic: Earnings proximity: cap the binary event

terms.definition: A structural force expected to run for years, backed by mathematical, physical or political necessity rather than opinion, that the macro thesis names and that capital has to flow toward. The framework allocates by force rather than by sector, and spreads each force across several economically distinct businesses.

source.ref: Part 5 · Portfolio Construction & Position Management; Part 2 · Lineage & Macro Thesis

appearsLater.topic: Allocate by force, not by sector

terms.definition: The highest price of the past 52 weeks. The framework reads a position's distance below it as one of three momentum dimensions: within 10 percent is healthy, 25 percent or more below is a correction, and 40 percent or more is severe distress (a doctrine target the dashboard does not yet measure).

source.ref: Part 5 · Portfolio Construction & Position Management; George & Hwang (2004), 'The 52-Week High and Momentum Investing', Journal of Finance 59(5)

terms.definition: How widely a move is shared across related names, read in the framework's momentum test as the share of them making new highs. Broad participation supports a thesis; narrowing leadership warns that a move is thinning even while the index holds (a doctrine target the dashboard does not yet measure).

Borrowing from your broker against the securities in your account instead of selling them. The framework treats it as an optional overlay, worth carrying only while the income it funds yields more than the borrow rate, and the broker can change its terms or call the loan under stress. A loan supplies cash without a sale, but it adds interest cost and the risk of a forced sale, which is a taxable event; Part 3's loan-to-value arithmetic shows how fast a falling market closes that gap.

source.ref: Part 4 · Tax Architecture & ROC Strategy (margin overlay); Part 3 · Bitcoin: Convexity Backbone (loan-to-value arithmetic, borrow phase)

terms.definition: A deliberate, documented and time-bounded departure from a default parameter, recorded with its reasons and the conditions under which it reverts. Drift that nobody wrote down does not count as an override; Part 5 calls it the signature of a framework being abandoned while its owner still believes in it.
The non-negotiable layer of the framework: the principles that define what it is. Changing one means no longer implementing the framework, as distinct from tuning a parameter or logging an override.
The strength of the evidence behind a position, as opposed to enthusiasm for it. The framework quantifies it through CIS so that size follows demonstrated evidence rather than feeling.
The prevailing structural conditions that determine how assets behave and correlate. The framework is built to adapt when the regime changes rather than to optimize for the average of all regimes.
Holding a position whose future paths include large upside without committing to which one occurs. It is the property CIS scores first, because it is what convexity is made of.
A payoff where the upside and downside are unequal in size or probability. The framework seeks it deliberately and treats symmetric risk measures as an incomplete description of survival.

The shared four-level register both scores read: seventy and above Strong, sixty to sixty-nine Moderate, fifty to fifty-nine Caution, below fifty Weak. On FIS seventy is also the action line; on CIS it is a band boundary, not an action trigger.

A cap on how far a score may move in a single update, scaled by how good the underlying evidence is. It forces a large re-rating to be earned across successive updates rather than granted in one enthusiastic week.
How much the evidence behind a score can support, derived by the engine from the quality of each source rather than asserted by hand. It sets how far a single update is allowed to move the score.
The structural class a position belongs to, which selects the lens CIS scores it through. It changes how the rubric is applied, never what the final number is floored at.

Starting a portfolio at one hundred and deducting a named penalty for each rule violation. Every point below one hundred is attributable to a specific departure, so the score reads as a repair list rather than a verdict.
The itemized account of which rule cost how many points. It is what makes a construction score actionable, because the fix is named alongside the deduction.
Capital held without a documented thesis or on a score nobody has refreshed. It is one of the five FIS penalty buckets, and it scales with position size.

Scaling a penalty by how large the offending position is, within a floor and a cap. A bigger position generates a proportionally bigger charge, but no single position is allowed to dominate the score.

The gap between the portfolio's actual posture mix and its target, which the market can open without a single trade. It is reported as a diagnostic alongside the score rather than billed as a penalty.
The record of what changed, why, and what would reverse it, written as the weekly loop closes. It is what makes the next week's pass a measurement rather than a memory.

Holding a deteriorating position because the story still sounds right. The framework names it as a failure mode of traditional portfolio management and answers it with quantified reassessment, so evidence rather than narrative decides whether a position stays.

source.ref: Part 1 — the failure modes the architecture addresses

appearsLater.topic: The failure modes the system answers

terms.definition: Missing a thesis break because there is more information than attention. The framework answers it with tripwires, which automate attention to the critical signals so a break is noticed when it happens rather than when it becomes convenient.

source.ref: Part 1 — the failure modes the architecture addresses

appearsLater.topic: The failure modes the system answers

terms.definition: The chance of a loss large enough to end compounding, which no later gain can repair. The framework treats ruin as a boundary condition rather than a risk to be traded off: survival comes first, because nothing compounds from zero.

source.ref: Taleb, Antifragile and The Black Swan; internal Part 2 lineage

terms.definition: The aggregate supply of money and credit in the system, read through measures such as M2 growth, central-bank balance sheets, and real rates. The framework treats its expansion and contraction as a tide that convex assets amplify rather than merely follow.

source.ref: Lyn Alden, liquidity-cycle work; internal Part 2 lineage

terms.definition: The reserve asset and principal source of convexity: a Bitcoin position held outside the three postures, accumulated on a schedule, governed by valuation discipline, and never sold, traded, or rebalanced. Liquidity comes from elsewhere.

source.ref: Part 3 — Bitcoin as the convexity backbone

terms.definition: Holding the Bitcoin reserve in hardware wallets under the holder’s own keys, accumulated through payroll contributions and held rather than trimmed on valuation. A custodian enters only if and when collateralized borrowing begins.

source.ref: Part 3 — TAM, custody, and the borrow phase

appearsLater.topic: Cold-storage architecture and the borrow phase

terms.definition: The handling rule for the backbone: Bitcoin is accumulated and never sold, traded, or rebalanced. Valuation models shape the pace of buying, not entries and exits, and cash needs are met from income, other assets, or borrowing against the reserve.

source.ref: Part 3 — Handling doctrine: accumulate, then borrow

terms.definition: The valuation read for Bitcoin: several independent models are compared, and their agreement is the signal. Convergence on undervaluation accelerates accumulation, convergence on overvaluation slows it, and wide divergence counsels holding the range.

source.ref: Part 3 — Why Bitcoin can be modeled

terms.definition: Bitcoin’s aggregate on-chain cost basis, with each coin valued at the price it last moved. It rises with adoption and marks a historically important bear-market regime level, not a hard floor: price can trade below it for extended stretches.

source.ref: Part 3 — Why Bitcoin can be modeled

terms.definition: Bitcoin’s share of the whole portfolio. A ten to fifteen percent target suits long horizons and moderate risk capacity, twenty to thirty percent suits higher conviction, and a mature thirty to fifty percent share can emerge over decades through accumulation rather than rebalancing.

source.ref: Part 3 — Reserve sizing by horizon and risk capacity

appearsLater.topic: Reserve sizing by horizon and risk capacity

terms.definition: A stretch in which Bitcoin trades well above its power-law trend and its realized-price basis. The response is to slow discretionary accumulation and build dry powder from income; an extension never prompts a sale of the reserve.

appearsLater.topic: Through two cycles: extension and convergence

terms.definition: The gap between a gross gain and what a given wrapper lets you keep after tax. It widens as the outcome grows, which is why the largest wins are the ones where wrapper placement matters most.

The only options use permitted inside a Roth: long calls, long puts, and defined-risk spreads, never undefined-risk strategies such as naked options or short volatility. A tactical overlay for a high-conviction thesis, capped at three to five percent of the account measured as maximum loss at entry.

appearsLater.topic: Options within the Roth: purchased convexity only

terms.definition: The portfolio boundary for every concentration rule: the total across all wrappers, including Roth, pre-tax, taxable, and Bitcoin cold storage. A position held in several accounts sums to one exposure, and the limits apply to that sum rather than to any single account.

source.ref: Part 5 — The portfolio boundary and single-name sleeves

appearsLater.topic: The portfolio boundary and single-name sleeves

terms.definition: A wrapper intentionally concentrated in one position, permitted only while the household aggregate stays inside its limits. The designation is explicit and documented, drift is monitored, and trimming is required if the aggregate breaches a cap. A governance structure, not an exception.

source.ref: Part 5 — The portfolio boundary and single-name sleeves

appearsLater.topic: The portfolio boundary and single-name sleeves

terms.definition: The truth problem, as distinct from the price problem: a core assertion behind a position has broken. Reassessment is immediate and price is irrelevant; a thesis-damaged position is downgraded or exited, and a later price recovery does not rehabilitate it.

source.ref: Part 5 — Thesis drift: price problems versus truth problems

appearsLater.topic: Thesis drift: price problems versus truth problems

terms.definition: The one to three claims a position depends on, written down at entry in a form that can be checked. They are what thesis drift is measured against: when one breaks, the position is reassessed on the evidence, whatever the price is doing.

source.ref: Part 5 — Protocol 05: one to three core assertions per position

appearsLater.topic: Protocol 05: one to three core assertions per position

terms.definition: A rule on the way in: a position down twenty percent or more from cost basis takes no new capital until a confirming signal arrives, such as a higher low, a reclaimed level, or new thesis-supporting evidence. Scaling in happens over weeks, with no more than a quarter of the target added in any one week.

source.ref: Part 5 — Adds and freezes: discipline on the way in

appearsLater.topic: Adds and freezes: discipline on the way in

terms.definition: The gate a position must pass before it can be Torque, and entry is earned three ways at once: a structural tailwind from an identifiable regime force, business survivability through stress without continuous access to capital markets, and valuation headroom large enough for a convex payoff, often five times or more. Passing earns a place, not a size.

source.ref: Part 5 — Torque: leverage on regime forces

terms.definition: A checklist, not an impression: a Ballast candidate must pass at least three of five tests covering a fortress balance sheet, diversified revenue, durable cash generation, low factor correlation, and a liquidity-resilient valuation. Yield is deliberately not on the list; income follows quality rather than qualifying it.

source.ref: Part 5 — Ballast: five tests, three required

terms.definition: The Hype exit schedule: one third of the position is sold at a fifty percent gain, another third at one hundred percent, and the remainder runs with the stop raised to breakeven. It converts a narrative trade into banked gains without pretending to know the top.

The middle layer of change governance: a threshold that may be tuned inside a documented envelope for an articulated reason, such as component weights, sizing bands, momentum thresholds, or concentration limits. Changing one adjusts the framework; changing doctrine abandons it.

The rule that every change to the rules is itself governed, by routing it to exactly one of three levels: doctrine, which cannot change without abandoning the framework; parameters, tunable within documented ranges; and overrides, temporary, documented, and time-bounded.

A state machine for stressed markets, when rising correlation and departing liquidity make positions that looked independent trade as one. The response is deliberately boring: pause new Torque adds, enforce posture limits strictly, consider trimming gross exposure by ten to twenty percent, and resume only after two calm weeks.

terms.definition: The heaviest CIS component at forty percent, because asymmetric upside is the objective. It scores TAM headroom, the optionality surface, catalyst density, and scarcity, each capped, summing to a 0 to 100 component score.

terms.definition: The CIS component, weighted twenty-five percent, that measures survivability under stress rather than price volatility: balance sheet, business-model fragility, factor correlation, and tail exposure. A higher score means lower fragility.

terms.definition: The CIS component, weighted twenty-five percent, that measures fit to the current regime rather than a forecast: regime sensitivity, carry direction, and policy alignment against the Part 2 thesis. A macro read may tilt a score; it is bounded so it can never determine one.

terms.definition: How much larger the addressable market is than the company, the first and largest sub-score inside Convexity and Optionality. It is scored on a logarithmic curve capped at thirty times, so the first multiple of headroom counts for far more than the twentieth.

terms.definition: A sub-score inside Convexity and Optionality that prices identifiable, dated reasons for a re-rating. Each catalyst earns points from its impact, probability, independence, evidence confidence, and time decay, so several versions of the same catalyst do not count twice.

terms.definition: The five named deductions FIS can take from one hundred: allocation, governance, dead capital, concentration, and complexity, each with its own cap. Because the caps sum to eighty, FIS can never fall below twenty, and every point lost names the rule that cost it.

The FIS reading of seventy: at or above it the portfolio holds, below it repair begins, with the attribution naming the fix. CIS reads the same four-band register, but there seventy is only the floor of the Strong band, a boundary rather than a trigger.

The ten-point signal on score movement. A CIS rise of ten points flags the position for resizing toward its larger target, a fall of ten flags a downsize, and either is paced over two to four weeks. Neither changes posture, which Part 5 governs, and neither alone forces an exit.

All CIS sub-scores are continuous values rather than bucketed tiers: a position scores 78.3, not 75 or 80. Continuity preserves the small week-over-week movement that longitudinal tracking exists to see.

The operating cadence, run Sunday evening or Monday pre-market: update CIS, calculate FIS, run the governance gates, act or deliberately hold, and log the evidence. It closes every week whether or not anything moved, which is what makes the next pass a measurement.

The four events that interrupt the weekly cadence rather than wait for it: a position moving more than five percent in one day, material news, an earnings announcement, or a tripwire condition met. Between triggers, frequency limits keep activity from passing for diligence.

Discipline includes doing nothing. A CIS or FIS change under five points is monitored, a position inside its band is not resized, and a week in which every check passed and nothing moved is the system working, not the system idle.

The failure CIS cannot see because it scores one position at a time: several high-scoring positions that move together under regime stress. Average correlation above 0.7 is flagged as a diagnostic; any penalty routes through FIS and governance, never through CIS.

A position whose score has quietly fallen while its sizing stayed put, because nobody recalculated: a thesis played out, a market compressed, catalysts exhausted. Scores stale past ninety days are flagged, and the dead-capital bucket bills them.
